steps.title: for acute heart failure
steps.instruction: for acute heart failure. (Table 1) Part 2 Systematic review and meta-analysis of early mobilization for acute heart failure Based on the scoping review above, we will design PICO and conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine the efficacy and safety of early mobilization for acute heart failure. (Table 2) P: Hospitalized acute heart failure patients I: Implement early mobilization (walking within three days or 72 hours of admission) C: Do not implement early mobilization O: Mortality, hospitalization days, readmission rates, ADL, mobility, quality of life, and adverse events (e.g., falls and changes in condition) associated with early mobilization 3.Method [Part 1] We describe this protocol that follows the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR) statement.16 We also use the scoping review framework by The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI)17 following the five stages approach as below. Stage 1: Identifying the research question We are interested in early mobilization for acute heart failure, and the research questions are as followed: 1. "What is the definition of early mobilization for acute heart failure?" 2. "When exactly is "early" in mobilization for acute heart failure?" 3. "What are the specific methods (implementation criteria, discontinuation criteria, frequency, time) of early mobilization for acute heart failure?" Stage 2: Identifying relevant studies We used the Population, Concept, and Context (PCC) framework17 to define the inclusion criteria as follows: Participants All publications that have been studied on acute heart failure will be included. The type of cardiovascular disease that causes acute heart failure is not relevant in this scoping review.

steps.title: Concept We will review the existing...
steps.instruction: Concept We will review the existing literature on early mobilization for acute heart failure regarding actual method, starting period, frequency and time. Context In this review, early mobilization is defined as "Activities such as sitting and walking that are started early after hospitalization". We will also include the study for early mobilization, early rehabilitation, and early physical therapy as defined by authors. Additionally, we will only use MEDLINE via Ovid to search for Part 1. We will include randomized controlled trials and observational study, and not apply language or country restrictions. We will exclude abstracts, letters, case series study and case reports without controls. We will not exclude studies based on the observation period or publication year. Stage 3: Study selection We will select studied following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA) flow diagram.18 We will use the PCC framework and the process will be carried out independently by two researchers (M.O. and H.O.). The two authors will compare their lists and any differences in opinion will be resolved by discussion and, where this fails, through arbitration by a third researcher (M.K.). Stage 4: Charting the data Data extraction will be carried out by one researcher (M.O.) using standard data extraction forms including diagnosis, design, setting, age, sample size, definition of mobilization, number of starting days defined as "early", start and stop criteria, frequency, time, and dropout rate. Another one researcher (H.O.) confirms the data extraction. If necessary, we will contact the authors of these studies. Stage 5: Collating, summarizing, and reporting the results We will present the results of the search in the PRISMA flow diagram. We will organize the extracted data described above as qualitative synthesis (Table 1). 3.Method [Part 2] 3.1 Protocol We used a systematic review protocol template (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.biqrkdv6). We

steps.title: followed the Preferred reporting items for...
steps.instruction: followed the Preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta-analysis protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015 for preparing this protocol.19 We will publish this protocol in protocols.io (https://www.protocols.io/). 3.2 Inclusion criteria of the articles for the review 3.2.1 Type of studies We will include randomized controlled trials and observational studies that assess the effectiveness and safety of early mobilization for hospitalized acute heart failure patients. In observational studies, comparisons will be made between the patients who have received early mobilization (walking a few days of admission, early mobilization group) and those who have not (control group). We will not apply language or country restrictions. We will include all papers including published, unpublished articles, abstract of conference and letter. We will exclude case series study and case reports without controls. We will not exclude studies based on the observation period or publication year. 3.2.2 Study participants We will include hospitalized patients with acute heart failure. The details of inclusion/exclusion criteria are as follows. Inclusion criteria: The criteria for heart failure follow Framingham's diagnostic criteria or the authors' definition. 18 years of age or older. Exclusion criteria: Patients who underwent surgical procedures or treatment with catheterization after hospitalization will be excluded. Patients who were unable to walk prior to admission should also be excluded. 3.2.3 Intervention Implement early mobilization: patients should start walking within three days or 72 hours of admission, with or without assistance or aids (cane, etc.)20,21. The definition for the number of days of walking initiation will use the definitions extracted from the scoping review. Additionally, protocol-based interventions with progressively increasing rehabilitation stages, including walking, are also defined as interventions. 3.2.4 Control

steps.title: Do not implement early mobilization
steps.instruction: Do not implement early mobilization: patients start walking after the above days of admission or do not walk. 3.3 Type of outcomes 3.3.1 Primary outcomes 1. Mortality Definition: Include both cardiovascular and other deaths. Period: During follow up period (use the longest follow-up period reported in the study) 2. Days of admission Definition: Number of days spent in the acute care hospital where the patient was first admitted Period: During follow up period 3. Readmission rate Definition: For readmissions, it doesn't matter if it is the same hospital where the patient was initially admitted. Period: During follow up period (use the longest follow-up period reported in the study) 3.3.2 Secondary outcomes 1. Activity of Daily Living (ADL) and mobility Definition: Handling data that assesses ADL and mobility (regardless of the type of assessment chart) Period: During follow up period (use the longest follow-up period reported in the study) 2. Quality of Life (QOL) Definition: Deals with patient assessed quality of life data (regardless of the type of assessment chart) Period: During follow up period (use the longest follow-up period reported in the study) 3. All adverse events Definition: Definition of adverse events are set by original authors. Incidence proportion of all adverse events Period: During follow up period (use the longest follow-up period reported in the study) 3.4 Search method 3.4.1 Electronic search

steps.title: We will search the following databases
steps.instruction: We will search the following databases: 1. the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL); 2. MEDLINE via Ovid; 3. EMBASE via ProQuest Dialog; 3. CINAHL; 4. PEDro; See Appendix 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 for the search strategies. 3.4.2 Other resources We will also search the following databases for ongoing or unpublished trials: 1. the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP); 2. ClinicalTrials.gov; See Appendix 6, 7 for the search strategies. We will check the reference lists of studies, including international guidelines22 as well as the reference lists of eligible studies and articles citing eligible studies. We will ask the authors of original studies for unpublished or additional data. 3.5 Data collection and analysis 3.5.1 Selection of the studies Three groups of two pairs (six reviewers in total, M.O., H.O., A.I., M.S., Y .S., and R.S.) will screen titles and abstracts, followed by the assessment of the eligibility based on the full texts. We will contact original authors if relevant data is missing. Disagreements between the two reviewers will be resolved by discussion, and if this fails, a third reviewer will act as an arbiter. 3.5.2 Data extraction and management Two reviewers will perform independent data extraction of the included studies using standardized data collection form. We will use a pre-checked form using 10 randomly selected studies. The form will include the information on study design, study population, interventions and outcomes (Table 1, Table 2). Any disagreements will be resolved by discussion, and if this fails, a third reviewer will act as an arbiter. We will ask the authors of original studies for unclear points. 3.6 Assessment of risk of bias in included studies Two reviewers will evaluate the risk of bias independently using the Risk of Bias 2 or ROBINS-I.23,24 Disagreements between the two reviewers will be discussed, and if this fails, a third reviewer will be acting as an arbiter, if necessary.

3.7 Measures of treatment effects We will pool the relative risk ratios/odds ratios and the 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the following binary variables: mortality, readmission rate. We will pool the mean differences and the 95% CIs for the following continuous variables: days of admission, ADL and mobility, QOL. If several different scales have been used in the included studies, we will pool the effect estimates using standard mean differences (SMDs). We will summarize adverse events based on the definition by the original article, but we will not perform meta-analysis. For studies with a defined start date for walking or rehabilitation, we will include only observational studies in the meta-analysis. In addition, for studies of protocol-based interventions, we will include only randomized controlled trials in the meta-analysis. We should conduct the two meta-analyses separately. 3.8 Unit of analysis issues Clustering at the level of the enrolled units in cluster randomized studies In dealing with cluster-RCTs, for dichotomous data, we will apply the design effect and calculate effective sample size and number of events using the intracluster correlation coefficient (ICC) among each unit and the average cluster size, as described in Chapter 16.3.5 of the Cochrane Handbook.25 If the ICC has not been reported, we will use the ICC of a similar study as a substitute. For continuous data, only the sample size will be reduced; means and standard deviation will remain unchanged.3 Randomized cross-over studies We will consider only data from the first period. Multiple comparisons All intervention groups that are relevant to this review will be included. 3.9 Handling of missing data We will ask not-presented data to the original authors. 3.9.1 Missing outcomes We will perform the intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for all dichotomous data as much as possible. For continuous data, we will not impute missing data based on the recommendation by Cochrane handbook.25 We will perform meta-analysis about the available data in the original study.

steps.title: Perform statistical and meta‑analysis steps
steps.instruction: 3.9.2 Missing statistics When original studies only report standard error or p-value, we will calculate the standard deviation based on the method by Altman.26 If we don't know these values when we contact the authors, standard deviation will be calculated by confidence interval and t-value based on the method by Cochrane handbook25, or validated method.26 Validity of these methods will be analyzed by sensitivity analysis. 3.10 Assessment of heterogeneity We will evaluate the statistical heterogeneity by visual inspection of the forest plots and calculating the I2 statistic (I2 values of 0% to 40%: might not be important; 30%to 60%: may represent moderate heterogeneity; 50% to 90%: may represent substantial heterogeneity; 75% to 100%: considerable heterogeneity). When there is substantial heterogeneity (I2> 50%), we will assess the reason for the heterogeneity. Cochrane Chi2test (Q-test) will be performed for I2 statistics, and P value less than 0.10 will be defined as statistically significant. 3.11 Assessment of reporting bias We will search the clinical trial registry system (ClinicalTrials.gov and ICTRP) and will perform extensive literature search for unpublished trials. We will assess the potential publication bias by visual inspection of the funnel plot. Egger test will be performed as well. We will not conduct the test when we find less than 10 trials or trials which have similar sample sizes. We will assess the potential publication bias by visual inspection of the funnel plot. 3.12 Meta-analysis Meta-analysis will be performed using Review Manager software (RevMan 5.4). We will use a random-effects model. 3.13 Subgroup analysis To elucidate the influence of effect modifiers on results, we will evaluate the subgroup analyses of the primary outcomes on the following factors when sufficient data are available. 1. (For participants) Over 65 years old and under 2. (For intervention) Early mobilization (walking) up to and after the second day of hospitalization 3.14 Sensitivity analysis We will undertake the following sensitivity analyses for the primary outcomes to assess whether the results of the review are robust to the decisions made during the review process. 1. Exclusion of studies using imputed statistics.

Undertake sensitivity analysis by excluding studies that used imputed statistics

steps.title: 2. Missing participants
steps.instruction: 2. Missing participants: verify the robustness of the results by seeking informative missingness odds ratios.27 3. Only the participants who complete the study with complete data 4. Inclusion of studies that have diagnosed heart failure with Framingham's diagnostic criteria or the authors' definition. Patients with heart failure who do not meet these criteria should be excluded. 5. For the main analysis, the definition extracted from the scoping review will be used for the criterion of early mobilization (the number of days starting from admission), but sensitivity analysis will be performed for the other days. 4. Summary of findings table Summary of findings table will be made for the following outcome based on the Cochrane handbook.25 We will include grading to evaluate the quality of evidence based on the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) approach for each Summary of findings table.28 1. Mortality 2. Hospital length of stay 3. Readmission ratio 4. ADL and mobility 5. QOL 6. All adverse events 5. Conflict of Interest The authors declare no conflicts of interests.
